metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Brings Breakout Momentum Into Week 7
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. enters Sunday's home matchup against the Miami Dolphins as a WR3/flex with real upside after his 48-yard score in Week 6. The rookie earned seven targets in his first game back from a four-game absence, catching six for 103 yards and a touchdown against the New England Patriots. Adonai Mitchell is returning from a finger injury, adding competition alongside Garrett Wilson. Cooper and Mitchell have appeared in the same game only in the season opener, when Cooper caught one pass for 30 yards, so his Week 6 workload came with a receiving group that will change again Sunday.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Could be set for lesser role
metadata.description: Cooper may get fewer looks in the passing game Sunday versus Miami with Adonai Mitchell cleared to return from a finger injury, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Cooper shined in his return from IR this past Sunday against New England, catching six of seven targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. That performance will likely gain him more attention from QB Geno Smith moving forward, but it must also be noted that Cooper's big game came in the absence of Mitchell, who is set to return Sunday following a four-game absence. Both Cooper and Mitchell are likely to remain behind Garrett Wilson in the pecking order, but it will be interesting to see if either Cooper or Mitchell is able to separate himself as the team's No. 2 wideout.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Emerging as a Priority Waiver-Wire Target
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. had the start of his NFL career delayed after he suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 that led to him being placed on Injured Reserve. However, the 22-year-old returned from IR with a bang in Week 6, recording six catches for 103 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. Cooper Jr. nearly had a second touchdown as well, if not for a questionable offensive pass interference penalty on fellow Jets wide receiver Tim Patrick that negated the score. The Jets could get back wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) from a finger injury in Week 7, which could impact Cooper Jr.'s playing time. Still, the rookie wideout looks to have an opportunity to establish himself as the WR2 in New York alongside star Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson. Where available, Cooper Jr. profiles as a priority waiver wire target for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Paces air attack in return
metadata.description: Cooper brought in six of seven targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Making his return from a four-game stint on injured reserve due to an ankle sprain suffered on the opening possession of the season, Cooper hit the ground running and finished as the team leader in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The Indiana product also recorded his first NFL touchdown on a 48-yard strike from Geno Smith early in the third quarter, and his instant production despite the layoff gives his fantasy outlook a significant boost heading into a Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. finds the end zone in Week 6 loss
metadata.description: Omar Cooper Jr. caught 6-of-7 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Cooper led the team in all receiving categories in the loss Sunday. Cooper had been out of action for the last four games with a high-ankle sprain. Cooper will look to continue to build rapport with QB Geno Smith in Week 7 against Miami.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Scores Touchdown in Week 6 Return
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. caught six of seven targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in his return to the gridiron in Week 6. The 30th-overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft missed the last four games with a high-ankle sprain, making it difficult for him to establish his role in a crowded receiver room. But Cooper seized the opportunity with Adonai Mitchell (finger) ruled out for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on Cooper in the coming weeks to see if he has consistent production or is better suited as a dynasty league stash.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Returning to action Week 6
metadata.description: Cooper (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Cooper will suit up for the first time since Week 1, when he sustained a high-ankle sprain on the Jets' first offensive possession of the season in an eventual win over the Titans. The rookie first-round pick out of Indiana returned to practice this week, turning in a pair of limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation Friday and getting activated from injured reserve Saturday. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for another week, Cooper could potentially settle in as the Jets' No. 2 receiver Sunday, pushing Tim Patrick down a spot on the depth chart.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Activated from IR
metadata.description: Cooper (ankle) was activated from injured reserve Saturday.
metadata.analysis: Cooper is still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots, but he's likely to be cleared to play given his activation from IR. The rookie fourth-rounder has missed the Jets' last four games due to an ankle injury, but he could be thrust into a prominent role offensively given the absence of Adonai Mitchell (finger).

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Set to be activated off IR
metadata.description: Cooper (ankle) is being activated from injured reserve Saturday and is expected to be available for Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Patriots, Connor Hughes of SNY TV reports.
metadata.analysis: Cooper earned the questionable tag for Week 6 after logging a full practice Friday, and it looks like the rookie first-rounder will be back on the field after spending the last four weeks on injured reserve due to an ankle injury he sustained against the Titans in Week 1. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) sidelined, Cooper could slide into the Jets' WR2 role behind Garrett Wilson for Sunday's contest.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Could Return to a Crowded Jets Receiving Group
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) could make his return against New England after missing the last four games with a high ankle sprain. Cooper caught one pass for 30 yards in the season opener before landing on injured reserve, and his absence has prevented him from building an established role in the Jets' offense. The rookie practiced fully Friday and is listed as questionable, although head coach Aaron Glenn has indicated that he expects Cooper to be available Sunday. New York would still need to activate him from injured reserve before he can play. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) ruled out, there is an opportunity for another receiver to earn playing time, but Cooper's workload after such a lengthy absence remains uncertain. His first-round draft pedigree makes him worth monitoring in dynasty formats and deeper redraft leagues, though he should remain on fantasy benches until his role becomes clearer.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Questionable for Week 6
metadata.description: Cooper (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at New England.
metadata.analysis: Cooper was a full practice participant Friday, upgrading from limited participation the previous two days. That doesn't necessarily mean he'll play, though the Jets definitely could use the help with Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for another week. They'll need to activate Cooper from injured reserve Friday or Saturday to have him available for Sunday's game against the Patriots at 1:00 p.m. ET.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Will practice fully Friday
metadata.description: Cooper (ankle) will be a full participant in Friday's practice, according to the Jets' official X account.
metadata.analysis: After logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, the rookie's upgrade to full participation is a positive step in his return from injured reserve. The Jets would need to activate Cooper on Friday or Saturday in order to have him available for Sunday's game at New England. It's not yet clear if the team intends to do that.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) to return in Week 6
metadata.description: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) will return for the Jets on Sunday against the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Cooper has not played since he was knocked out of the Jets' season opener with a sprained ankle. The first-round rookie has returned to limited practice sessions this week, and it was announced Friday morning that he's ready for in-game action. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) remaining out this week, Cooper should slot right in behind Garrett Wilson at wide receiver for the Jets. However, there is certainly a chance that Cooper is eased back into the mix as far as total snaps go.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Set to Play Against Patriots
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was a full participant in Friday's practice and is set to play against the New England Patriots on Sunday, according to Ian Rapoport. The first-round rookie has been sidelined since injuring his ankle in the season opener against Tennessee, where he caught one pass for 30 yards before exiting after five offensive snaps. Cooper returned to practice Wednesday after the Jets opened his 21-day window to come off injured reserve, then logged limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday. He must be activated to the active roster before kickoff. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) also ruled out, Cooper could see immediate playing time, although his workload remains uncertain after a five-week absence. His return gives New York another option in the passing game, but fantasy managers should leave him on the bench until his role becomes clearer.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) logs limited practice Thursday
metadata.description: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) logged a limited practice session on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie was able to participate in Thursday's practice in a limited fashion. He is drawing close to a return from the ankle injury that left him on injured reserve, but it's still unclear whether or not his return will come in time for Sunday's divisional matchup against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Stays limited in practice
metadata.description: Cooper (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Cooper had his reps capped for the second day in a row after the Jets designated him for return from injured reserve Wednesday. The Jets will have just under three weeks to reinstate Cooper, so the rookie wideout may need to upgrade to full participation in Friday's session to have a shot at suiting up this weekend versus the Patriots. Cooper recorded a 30-yard reception and played just five snaps before exiting his NFL debut Week 1 against the Titans in the first quarter due to a high-ankle sprain.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) practices Thursday
metadata.description: Omar Cooper Jr. practiced again on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Cooper was designated to return to practice on Wednesday where he was limited. It is unclear if he has a chance to return on Sunday.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) officially limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie has been out for over four weeks due to an ankle injury, but he recently had his practice window opened up and was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday. It looks like he will be back in the lineup in the near future, although it's unclear whether or not his return will come in Week 6.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Limited in return to practice
metadata.description: Cooper (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: After being designated for return from injured reserve earlier Wednesday, Cooper operated with a cap on his reps in his first practice since he exited the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans due to a high-ankle sprain. The Jets haven't ruled out the possibility of the rookie first-round pick being activated from IR in advance of Sunday's game against the Patriots, but he'll likely need to practice fully Thursday and/or Friday to have a realistic chance at suiting up this weekend.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has practice window opened
metadata.description: The Jets are opening WR Omar Cooper Jr's 21-day practice window.
metadata.analysis: Cooper was placed on IR after Week 1 with a high-ankle sprain. He will be activated within the next few weeks.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Making return to practice Wednesday
metadata.description: The Jets designated Cooper (ankle) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
metadata.analysis: Cooper is slated to participate in Wednesday's walk-through practice in some capacity after the Jets opened his 21-day evaluation window. The rookie first-round pick -- who was deactivated after sustaining a high-ankle sprain in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans -- could have a chance at returning to action as soon as this Sunday at New England, depending on how he fares in practice this week. With the Jets classifying fellow wideout Adonai Mitchell (finger) as week-to-week, Cooper could have a chance at reclaiming a notable role in the receiving corps once he's activated from IR.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Returning to Practice on Wednesday
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie first-round wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle), who is on Injured Reserve, will practice on Wednesday, head coach Aaron Glenn told Connor Hughes of SNY. It is good news for the Jets, but it does not guarantee that Cooper will be activated from IR to play this weekend on the road against the division-rival New England Patriots in Week 6. The 22-year-old from Indiana sprained his ankle in his NFL debut in the Week 1 win over the Tennessee Titans after catching his only target for a 30-yard gain. Cooper, who is rostered in only 3% of Yahoo leagues while recovering from his ankle sprain, could quickly become involved in New York's passing game when he returns, especially since Adonai Mitchell (finger) has missed the last couple of games due to injury. In deeper fantasy formats, Cooper is definitely worth a speculative stash for WR depth for his upside in an improved Jets offense.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Worth a Look as Week 6 Eligibility Nears
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is still on injured reserve, but the rookie is getting closer to being eligible to return. Cooper sprained his ankle in Week 1 against Tennessee and was placed on IR on Sept. 19, keeping him out through Sunday's game against Cleveland. Week 6 at New England is the earliest he can play, although the Jets haven't announced a timetable. The first-round pick played only five offensive snaps in his debut but turned his lone target into a 30-yard catch-and-run. New York's receiving situation has changed somewhat during his absence. Adonai Mitchell (finger) has missed two straight games and hasn't practiced this week, while Isaiah Williams has taken on more work. Tim Patrick has also returned to practice after opening the season on injured reserve. Cooper was selected 30th overall and should eventually get an opportunity to compete for meaningful snaps, but his role upon returning remains uncertain. He's worth considering as an IR stash in deeper fantasy leagues, particularly for managers who can afford to wait.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Officially on injured reserve
metadata.description: The Jets placed Cooper (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Cooper thus will miss at least the next four games after he suffered a sprained ankle in his pro debut this past Sunday in Tennessee. His next chance for game action will be a Week 6 road matchup with the Patriots on Sunday, Oct. 18, and in the meantime, the Jets will operate with a receiving corps composed of Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Isaiah Williams and Arian Smith.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) placed on injured reserve
metadata.description: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been placed on injured reserve and will be sidelined for at least four weeks.
metadata.analysis: The Jets are placing their first-round rookie on injured reserve after he suffered an ankle injury in his NFL debut last week. He is going to miss at least four weeks as a result, but he's not expected to be out much beyond that. Adonai Mitchell and Kenyon Sadiq will both see increased opportunities in his absence for the next few weeks at least.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - To be placed on injured reserve
metadata.description: The Jets are expected to place Cooper (ankle) on injured reserve, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Cooper suffered a sprained ankle early on in his pro debut this past Sunday at Tennessee that left him week-to-week. He predictably didn't practice during Week 2 prep and then was ruled out ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Packers. Once he's officially on injured reserve, Cooper will need to miss at least the next four games, at which point New York will be able to designate him for return from IR. In the meantime, Isaiah Williams figures to take on a bigger role behind Garrett Williams and Adonai Mitchell.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Heading to Injured Reserve
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is going to be put on Injured Reserve, sources told Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. The move will give Cooper four weeks to recover from the ankle sprain that he suffered in the Week 1 season-opening win over the Tennessee Titans. The earliest that Cooper will be able to return will be on Oct. 18 on the road against the division-rival New England Patriots. The 22-year-old 30th overall pick from Indiana is not a must-stash in 12- and 14-team leagues while he recovers. Before injuring his ankle last Sunday, Cooper caught his only target for a 30-yard gain. With Cooper sidelined for at least the next four games, top wideout Garrett Wilson will have a larger target share from quarterback Geno Smith, while Adonai Mitchell should also become a much more attractive sleeper as a WR4/flex, beginning in Week 2 against the visiting Green Bay Packers.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Ruled out for Week 2
metadata.description: Cooper (ankle) will not play Sunday against the Packers, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: It was reported earlier this week that Cooper was week-to-week with the ankle injury he sustained in Week 1, so it comes as little surprise that he will sit out his team's second game of the season. Isaiah Williams is the favorite to pick up extra snaps in Cooper's absence.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Ruled Out for Week 2
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) will not play Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, according to Zack Rosenblatt. Cooper sat out practice Wednesday and Thursday after being labeled week-to-week earlier in the week, so the rookie will miss at least one game. He made an impact before getting hurt in the opener, turning his only target into a 30-yard gain that set up New York's first touchdown. Cooper played just five offensive snaps before leaving. The MRI brought encouraging news, and the hope remains that he can return within four weeks, though there is no firm timetable yet. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell remain atop the receiver group, while Isaiah Williams played 40 offensive snaps in Week 1 and should stay involved with Cooper unavailable.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) absent from practice Thursday
metadata.description: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was absent from practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie has yet to be officially ruled out for Week 2, but that will certainly happen, as his recovery timeline is not day-to-day and he hasn't practiced all week. Expect Adonai Mitchell and Kenyon Sadiq to benefit from his absence for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper - Sidelined in practice as expected
metadata.description: Cooper (ankle) didn't practice Thursday after also missing Wednesdays practice.
metadata.analysis: Cooper's inability to practice is no surprise considering he's expected to miss multiple weeks due to an ankle sprain he sustained in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans. Prior to getting hurt in the first quarter of his NFL debut, the rookie first-round pick had a 30-yard catch and run. Expect Cooper to be ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers when the Jets release game statuses Friday.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. Doesn't Practice on Wednesday
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) did not suit up for Wednesday's practice session. As expected, Cooper didn't practice to begin the week after sustaining an ankle sprain during Sunday's season opener. The Jets expected Cooper to miss several weeks while he recovers from his sprained ankle. The absence of Cooper could mean that Adonai Mitchell and tight end Kenyon Sadiq see larger roles in the passing game during the Week 2 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. Fantasy managers should place Cooper on their IR and hope that he returns relatively soon.

metadata.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) misses practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) missed New York's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, the rookie did not suit up or take part in New York's practice on Wednesday. He is expected to miss several weeks while tending to an ankle injury, so fantasy managers should expect more work for Adonai Mitchell and Kenyon Sadiq for the foreseeable future.
